enforcement_note: DENY. guard_force_push parses the push, resolves the destination refspec and blocks only when it names a protected branch, so force-pushing a topic branch you own still works - which a `permissions.deny` pattern could not express. Three limits, stated so `live` is not read as unbypassable: the dispatcher is fail-soft, so an exception in the handler allows the call; the guard only sees Bash and PowerShell tool calls, not a terminal opened outside Claude Code; and it splits on shell separators without honouring quotes, so a separator inside a quoted string can produce a false positive.
rule: Never force-push to a shared or protected branch.
ai_action: If a force-push to main or any shared branch is requested, HALT and explain the alternative (a new commit, or a force-push to your own topic branch after confirming nobody else has pulled it).
